core_obligations: Produce alpha: set r equal to the dimension over kappa(p) of N tensor_S kappa(p) and map the free module of rank r onto N by sending the standard basis to a chosen basis of that vector space; this proves existence (proof lines 3171-3176).

Reduce to one implication: for a fixed alpha apply the algebraic induction step to alpha localised at r to get that (1), (3), (4), (5) and (6) are equivalent, and note that (2) trivially implies (3), so it remains to prove that (1) implies (2) (proof lines 3178-3186).

Prove (1) implies (2): assuming N_q flat over R, the flat locus U_1 is open and contains q and p, the isomorphism locus U_2 is open because the modules are finitely presented and contains p, and Phi : Spec(S) -> Spec(R) is open because R -> S is flat and finitely presented; then for every prime r' in Phi(U_1 intersect U_2) there is a prime over it where N is flat and alpha is an isomorphism, so alpha tensored with kappa(p') is an isomorphism and alpha_{r'} is universally injective by (1) implies (3); choosing f outside r with D(f) inside Phi(U_1 intersect U_2) makes alpha_f universally injective over R_f, and the same reasoning shows the cokernel of alpha is R-flat at every prime of U_1 intersect Phi^{-1}(Phi(U_1 intersect U_2)), a set containing q, so a suitable g outside q finishes (proof lines 3188-3225).
proof_roadmap: Construct the map alpha from a basis of the fibre at p (proof lines 3171-3176).
Use the algebraic induction step to reduce to the single implication (1) implies (2) (proof lines 3178-3186).
Assume flatness at q and use the three openness statements to exhibit f and g as required (proof lines 3188-3225).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the induction step of the flatterling theory over a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres: it produces a map from a finite free module to a finitely presented module that is an isomorphism on the special fibre, and shows that the flatness of the localisation at a prime over r is equivalent to five other conditions, one of which is the existence of localised elements making the map universally injective with flat cokernel (statement lines 3140-3169, tag 05IA). The proof constructs alpha from a basis of the fibre, then reduces the six conditions to one implication via the algebraic induction step, and that implication requires combining openness of the flat locus, openness of the isomorphism locus for a map of finitely presented modules, and openness of the image of a flat finitely presented ring map to produce the two localising elements. The openness argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
